chunks: Abdul Wahid ibn Abdullah ibn Yunus narrated to us, he said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Rabah narrated to us, he said: He narrated to me Ahmad ibn Ali al-Himyari, from al-Hasan ibn Ayyub, from Abdul Kareem ibn Amr al-Khath'ami, from Ahmad ibn al-Harith, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said: I heard him say - meaning Abu Abdullah (as):
Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir (as) said: When the Qa'im (as) rises, he will say:
So I fled from you when I feared you, then my Lord granted me wisdom and made me of the messengers.

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far (title for Imam al-Baqir as)
key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdullah (title for Imam al-Sadiq as)
key_terms.الْقَائِمُ: The Rising One (title for the Twelfth Imam)

ai.seo_question: What Quranic verse does the Qa'im recite upon rising?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (as) links the emergence of the Qa'im to the Quranic narrative of Prophet Hud, specifically citing Surah Hud 11:46 to illustrate the transition from concealment to public mission. This reference underscores the theological continuity between the Imams and the Prophets, framing the Mahdi's rise as a divinely ordained restoration of authority following a period of waiting and fear. The citation highlights the spiritual legitimacy of the Imam's leadership as an extension of prophetic tradition.
